results.original_statement_md: Given the input $\mathbf x\in\mathcal X$ and the target label $y\in\mathcal Y$, the DNN is learned to map $\mathbf x$ to $y$. Layerwise transformations can be roughly represented by $$y=g(z),\quad z=W_{L+1}\cdots\boldsymbol\sigma_2(W_2\boldsymbol\sigma_1(W_1\mathbf x+b_1)+b_2)\cdots+b_{L+1}.\tag{1}$$ Here $g$ is an optional top layer such as softmax; the module before it is piecewise linear. For a given input, the transformation is $z=W\mathbf x+b$, where $W=W_{L+1}\boldsymbol\sigma_LW_L\cdots\boldsymbol\sigma_2W_2\boldsymbol\sigma_1W_1$ and $b$ is the equivalent bias. Different inputs can generate different gate matrices and hence different $W,b$.
results.original_proof_md:
In this section, we further discuss gating states of different gating layers, which is mentioned in Section 3 of the paper. Let $\mathbf h_l\triangleq W_l(\boldsymbol\sigma_{l-1}(W_{l-1}\ldots(W_2\boldsymbol\sigma_1(W_1\mathbf x+\mathbf b_1)+\mathbf b_2)\cdots+\mathbf b_{l-1}))+\mathbf b_l$ denote the input of the $l$-th gating layer. We consider the vectorized form of $\mathbf h_l$. Given $\mathbf h_l\in\mathbb R^D$, the formulation of $\boldsymbol\sigma_l$ in different gating layers is given as follows.

(1) ReLU layer. In this case, $\boldsymbol\sigma_l=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_l^1,\sigma_l^2,\ldots,\sigma_l^D)\in\{0,1\}^D$, which is a diagonal matrix. If the $d$-th dimension of $\mathbf h_l$ is larger than $0$, then we have $\sigma_l^d=1$; otherwise, $\sigma_l^d=0$.

(2) Dropout layer. In this case, $\boldsymbol\sigma_l=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_l^1,\sigma_l^2,\ldots,\sigma_l^D)\in\{0,1\}^D$, which is a diagonal matrix. If the $d$-th dimension of $\mathbf h_l$ is not dropped, then we have $\sigma_l^d=1$; otherwise, $\sigma_l^d=0$.

(3) Max-Pooling layer. Since a pooling layer may change the size of the input, $\boldsymbol\sigma_l$ is not necessarily a square matrix. Let the output of the max-pooling layer be $\boldsymbol\sigma_l\mathbf h_l\in\mathbb R^{D'}$, i.e. the input $\mathbf h_l$ is divided into $D'$ regions. In this case, we have $\boldsymbol\sigma_l\in\{0,1\}^{D'\times D}$. If $(\mathbf h_l)_{d'}$ is the largest element in the $d'$-th region, then we have $(\boldsymbol\sigma_l)_{d'd}=1$; otherwise, $(\boldsymbol\sigma_l)_{d'd}=0$.

proof_steps.title: 连接真实ReLU网络与门区域
proof_steps.body_md: 实际网络递推先求预激活$W_jt_j+b_j$再逐坐标max(0,·)。固定门区域只要求这些真实预激活的门等于所选$s_j$，不假设网络已等于仿射式。逐层用ReLU门恒等式并归纳，得到实际输出等于冻结门的仿射链；再加入原最后无门线性层，其偏置同样保留。

proof_steps.title: 固定真实 dropout 的坐标作用
proof_steps.body_md: 原 Appendix A 的保留位 $k_d\in\{0,1\}$ 给真实输出 $D_k(h)_d=k_dh_d$。Boolean keep 的 public dropoutLinear 正是保留坐标或置零；分别检查保留/删除两支，得到加法与标量乘法保持。故 $D_k(Wx+b)=(D_k\circ W)x+D_k(b)$，偏置同样被门作用，不被丢掉。这里固定的是实际采样所得 keep 位，不假定带随机门的整个网络全局仿射。

proof_steps.title: 从真实最大池化构造一个最大者选择
proof_steps.body_md: 每个输出窗口 $R_p$ 是非空有限输入索引集，真实池化值为 $M(h)_p=\max_{d\in R_p}h_d$。有限最大值存在且达到，public maximizingSelector 为每个窗口选择一个达到最大值的输入，允许并列。于是 $M(h)_p=h_{a(p)}$，不是在并列时把多个最大值相加。固定门区域要求同一 $a(p)\in R_p$ 对该真实预激活仍最大；证明有限 sup 等于选择值后，得到 $M(Wx+b)=(P_a\circ W)x+P_a(b)$。这些真实算子的线性作用可吸收到此前仿射链的权重/偏置，layer_comp 继续保留末层偏置。原 Appendix A 的池化输入下标笔误另列，不改作者式。

en.title: Affine transformation at fixed gates
en.overview: The coordinate identity $\max(0,h_d)=1_{h_d>0}h_d$ gives a diagonal ReLU gate. Dropout fixes a binary mask; pooling selects an index attaining the maximum in each window, with any maximizer allowed at a tie. The action of this fixed gate pattern is linear.

assumptions.body_md: A finite chain may have different layer widths. Fix the ReLU/dropout/pooling selection matrices actually triggered by the input, with compatible linear maps and biases. The optional softmax $g$ is outside the affine-module conclusion.

definitions.body_md: Absorb fixed gates into the adjacent linear maps $A_j$ and write $t_{j+1}=A_jt_j+b_j$. Let $F_j$ be the first j affine layers, with $F_0(x)=x$.

proof_steps.title: Fix the linear gate action
proof_steps.body_md: The coordinate identity $\max(0,h_d)=1_{h_d>0}h_d$ gives a diagonal ReLU gate. Dropout fixes a binary mask; pooling selects an index attaining the maximum in each window, with any maximizer allowed at a tie. The action of this fixed gate pattern is linear.

proof_steps.title: Compose the linear part and bias
proof_steps.body_md: If $F_j(x)=B_jx+c_j$, then $F_{j+1}(x)=A_jB_jx+A_jc_j+b_j$. Induction covers any finite depth and varying widths. The equivalent bias is $F_L(0)$; the original network bias is retained.

proof_steps.title: Connect actual ReLU evaluation to the gate region
proof_steps.body_md: The actual network first computes the preactivation $W_jt_j+b_j$ and then applies coordinate-wise max(0,·). A fixed gate region requires only that gates of these actual preactivations equal the selected $s_j$, without assuming affine output. The ReLU gate identity and induction identify actual evaluation with the frozen-gate affine chain. Adding the source final ungated linear layer preserves its bias.

proof_steps.title: Freeze the actual coordinate action of dropout

The actual sampled keep bits are frozen; no globally affine network with varying random gates is assumed.

proof_steps.title: Construct one maximizing selector from actual max pooling
proof_steps.body_md: Each output window $R_p$ is a nonempty finite set of input indices, with actual pool value $M(h)_p=\max_{d\in R_p}h_d$. A finite maximum is attained; public maximizingSelector chooses one attaining input per window, including ties. Thus $M(h)_p=h_{a(p)}$, without adding tied maxima. A fixed gate region requires the same $a(p)\in R_p$ to maximize the actual preactivation. Proving that the finite supremum equals its selected value yields $M(Wx+b)=(P_a\circ W)x+P_a(b)$. These actual linear actions are absorbed into the preceding affine chain weights and biases; layer_comp retains the final bias. The source pooling input-index slip remains separately recorded.

assumptions.body_md: 原网络的门变量有限离散，所有条件/联合律来自同一分布；层前缀/后缀使用相同样本，不要求每个门模式出现。

definitions.body_md: 有限门/标签联合律$p$满足$p\ge0$、$\sum p=1$。定义$H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$、$H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$；$p_a=0$整行贡献0，不要求全支撑正质量。

results.original_statement_md: $H(\Sigma)$ is the entropy of gating states among all inputs, measuring the complexity of transformations encoded in gating layers. The complexity can be decomposed as $$H(\Sigma)=H(\Sigma_1)+H(\Sigma_2\mid\Sigma_1)+\cdots+H(\Sigma_L\mid\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{L-1}).$$
results.overview: 正边缘质量的行满足$p(a,b)=p(a)p(b\mid a)$；逐项分解$-p(a,b)\log p(a,b)$并求和。零边缘质量迫使该行所有联合原子为0，因此贡献0。

results.title: Property1：确定性门的三元信息非负

assumptions.body_md: 无额外采样/dropout；给定所指输入或中间特征后，所指全部后继门由固定网络确定。标签有限，概率核可测；输入/中间特征可连续。

definitions.body_md: 有限门/标签联合律$p$满足$p\ge0$、$\sum p=1$。定义$H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$、$H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$；$p_a=0$整行贡献0，不要求全支撑正质量。
输入$X$可在任意可测空间取值，分布为$\mu$。无额外采样/dropout时门是确定性$f(X)$；标签条件律$k_x(y)=P(Y=y\mid X=x)$与门来自同一概率模型。$p(y,\sigma)=\int1_{f(x)=\sigma}k_x(y)d\mu(x)$，原子概率核可测。
采用原作者co-information约定$ I(X;\Sigma;Y)=I(\Sigma;Y)-I(\Sigma;Y\mid X)$。其中条件MI是$\int I(k_x(y)1_{f(x)=\sigma})d\mu(x)$。只使用有限标签/门的熵，不要求连续$X$存在离散Shannon熵。

results.original_statement_md: Property 1. If the DNN does not introduce information besides the input $X$ (e.g. there is no sampling operations or dropout operations throughout the DNN), we have $I(X;\Sigma;Y)\ge0$.
results.original_proof_md:
This section proves the three properties mentioned in Section 3 of the paper, and also gives detailed proofs for other important conclusions in the paper.

Proof. Recall that the mutual information is defined as

$$\begin{aligned}
I(X;\Sigma;Y)&=I(X;Y)-I(X;Y\mid\Sigma)\\
&=(H(Y)-H(Y\mid X))-(H(Y\mid\Sigma)-H(Y\mid X,\Sigma))\\
&=(H(Y)-H(Y\mid\Sigma))-(H(Y\mid X)-H(Y\mid X,\Sigma)).
\end{aligned}\tag{6}$$

If the DNN does not introduce additional information besides $X$, which means that $\Sigma$ is determined by $X$, then we have $H(Y\mid X)-H(Y\mid X,\Sigma)=I(\Sigma;Y\mid X)=0$. Therefore,

$$I(X;\Sigma;Y)=H(Y)-H(Y\mid\Sigma)\ge0.\tag{7}$$

en.title: Property 1: nonnegative three-way information for deterministic gates
en.overview: Combine the conditional label kernel with the deterministic gate and integrate over the input law: $p(y,\sigma)=\int k_x(y)1_{f(x)=\sigma}d\mu$. Nonnegativity and total mass one follow from the conditional law at each input and interchange of a finite sum with the integral.

assumptions.body_md: There is no additional sampling/dropout. The specified input or intermediate feature determines all specified subsequent gates in the fixed network. Labels are finite and atom kernels measurable; input and intermediate features may be continuous.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

The input may take values in any measurable space with law $\mu$. Without additional sampling/dropout, the gate is deterministic $f(X)$. The conditional label law $k_x(y)=P(Y=y\mid X=x)$ belongs to the same probability model. The joint law is $p(y,\sigma)=\int1_{f(x)=\sigma}k_x(y)d\mu(x)$, with measurable atom kernels.

Use the author co-information convention $ I(X;\Sigma;Y)=I(\Sigma;Y)-I(\Sigma;Y\mid X)$. Conditional MI is $\int I(k_x(y)1_{f(x)=\sigma})d\mu(x)$. Only finite label/gate entropy is used; a discrete Shannon entropy of continuous input is unnecessary.

results.original_proof_md:
• $H(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l)\le H(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1})$.

Proof.

$$\begin{aligned}
&H(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l)-H(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1})\\
&=-H(\Sigma_{l+1}\mid\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l)\\
&=\mathbb E_{\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_{l+1}}[\log p(\sigma_{l+1}\mid\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_l)]\\
&\le0.
\end{aligned}\tag{8}$$

results.original_statement_md: • $I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_1\})\le I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1}\})$.
results.original_proof_md:
• $I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_1\})\le I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1}\})$.

Proof. If the DNN does not introduce additional information besides the input during the forward propagation, then $\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l,\Sigma_{l+1}$ are all determined by $X$, thereby $H(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\mid X)=H(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1}\mid X)=0$. Therefore,

$$\begin{aligned}
&I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\})-I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1}\})\\
&=(H(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l)-H(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\mid X))-(H(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1})-H(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1}\mid X))\\
&=H(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l)-H(\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1})\\
&\le0.
\end{aligned}\tag{9}$$

results.original_proof_md:
• $H(\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L)\ge H(\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L)$.

Proof.

$$\begin{aligned}
&H(\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L)-H(\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L)\\
&=H(\Sigma_l\mid\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L)\\
&=-\mathbb E_{\sigma_l,\ldots,\sigma_L}[\log p(\sigma_l\mid\sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\sigma_L)]\\
&\ge0.
\end{aligned}\tag{12}$$

results.original_statement_md: • $I(T_{l-1};\{\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L\})\ge I(T_l;\{\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L\})$.
results.original_proof_md:
• $I(T_{l-1};\{\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L\})\ge I(T_l;\{\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L\})$.

Proof. If the DNN does not introduce additional information besides the input during the forward propagation, then $\Sigma_l,\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L$ are all determined by $T_{l-1}$, thereby $H(\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L\mid T_{l-1})=0$. Therefore,

$$\begin{aligned}
&I(T_{l-1};\{\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L\})-I(T_l;\{\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L\})\\
&=(H(\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L)-H(\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L\mid T_{l-1}))-(H(\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L)-H(\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L\mid T_l))\\
&=H(\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L)-H(\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L)\\
&\ge0.
\end{aligned}\tag{13}$$

results.original_statement_md: • $I(T_{l-1};\{\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L\};Y)\ge I(T_l;\{\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L\};Y)$.
results.original_proof_md:
• $I(T_{l-1};\{\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L\};Y)\ge I(T_l;\{\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L\};Y)$.

Proof. According to Eq. (7), if there is no additional information besides the input throughout the DNN, then

$$I(T_{l-1};\{\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L\};Y)=H(Y)-H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L\}).\tag{14}$$

We can obtain the following inequality:

$$\begin{aligned}
&I(T_{l-1};\{\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L\};Y)-I(T_l;\{\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L\};Y)\\
&=(H(Y)-H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L\}))-(H(Y)-H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L\}))\\
&=H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L\})-H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_l,\ldots,\Sigma_L\})\\
&=I(\Sigma_l;Y\mid\{\Sigma_{l+1},\ldots,\Sigma_L\})\\
&\ge0.
\end{aligned}\tag{15}$$

$$I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\};Y)=H(Y)-H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\}).\tag{10}$$

We can obtain the following inequality:

$$\begin{aligned}
&I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\};Y)-I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1}\};Y)\\
&=(H(Y)-H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\}))-(H(Y)-H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1}\}))\\
&=H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1}\})-H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\})\\
&=-I(\Sigma_{l+1};Y\mid\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\})\\
&\le0.
\end{aligned}\tag{11}$$

assumptions.body_md: There is no additional sampling/dropout. The specified input or intermediate feature determines all specified subsequent gates in the fixed network. Labels are finite and atom kernels measurable; input and intermediate features may be continuous.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

The input may take values in any measurable space with law $\mu$. Without additional sampling/dropout, the gate is deterministic $f(X)$. The conditional label law $k_x(y)=P(Y=y\mid X=x)$ belongs to the same probability model. The joint law is $p(y,\sigma)=\int1_{f(x)=\sigma}k_x(y)d\mu(x)$, with measurable atom kernels.

Use the author co-information convention $ I(X;\Sigma;Y)=I(\Sigma;Y)-I(\Sigma;Y\mid X)$. Conditional MI is $\int I(k_x(y)1_{f(x)=\sigma})d\mu(x)$. Only finite label/gate entropy is used; a discrete Shannon entropy of continuous input is unnecessary.

results.original_statement_md: For DNNs with similar activation rates, we prove the negative correlation between complexity $H(\Sigma_l)$ and entanglement $TC(\Sigma_l)$ (proof in Appendix B.4): $$H(\Sigma_l)+TC(\Sigma_l)=C_l,\qquad C_l=\sum_dH_{l,d},\tag{2}$$ where $H_{l,d}=-a_{l,d}\log a_{l,d}-(1-a_{l,d})\log(1-a_{l,d})$. We can roughly consider $C_l$ as a constant if the average activation rate over all dimensions $\{a_{l,d}\mid1\le d\le D\}$ in the l-th layer converges to a certain number.
results.original_proof_md:
• $H(\Sigma_l)$

Proof.

$$\begin{aligned}
H(\Sigma_l)+TC(\Sigma_l)&=H(\Sigma_l)+KL\left(p(\sigma_l)\Big\|\prod_d p(\sigma_l^d)\right)\\
&=\mathbb E_{\sigma_l}\left[\log\frac1{p(\sigma_l)}\right]+\mathbb E_{\sigma_l}\left[\log\frac{p(\sigma_l)}{\prod_d p(\sigma_l^d)}\right]\\
&=-\mathbb E_{\sigma_l}\left[\log\prod_d p(\sigma_l^d)\right]\quad\text{\\\\ }p(\sigma_l^d)\text{ does not depend on the input}\\
&=C_l.
\end{aligned}\tag{16}$$

Let us consider DNNs with similar activation rates $a_l^d$. Because $p(\sigma_l^d)$ follows the Bernoulli distribution with the activation rate $a_l^d$, for DNNs with similar activation rates $a_l^d$, they share similar values of $C_l$. In this case, there is a negative correlation between $H(\Sigma_l)$ and $TC(\Sigma_l)$.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

definitions.body_md: 有限门/标签联合律$p$满足$p\ge0$、$\sum p=1$。定义$H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$、$H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$；$p_a=0$整行贡献0，不要求全支撑正质量。

一般随机门用真实条件核$K_x(y,\sigma)=P(Y=y,\Sigma_l=\sigma\mid X=x)$，不要求Σ由X唯一决定。实际联合律$p(y,\sigma)=\int K_x(y,\sigma)d\mu$；门条件熵$H(\Sigma_l\mid X)=\int H(K_x^\Sigma)d\mu$，$H(\Sigma_l\mid X,Y)=\int H_{K_x}(\Sigma_l\mid Y)d\mu$。有限输出熵可测且有界，故积分可交换相减。
对二值门向量定义边缘$p_d$、$TC(p)=D_{KL}(p\Vert\prod_dp_d)$、$C=\sum_dH(p_d)$。$TC(\Sigma\mid Y)=\sum_yp_yTC(p(\Sigma\mid y))$，$C_{\mid Y}=\sum_yp_y\sum_dH(p(\Sigma^d\mid y))$。正联合原子使对应边缘原子正，KL在真支撑上可定义。

results.original_statement_md: Furthermore, we extend conclusions in Equation (2) and prove that the negative correlation between complexity and entanglement still holds true for $I(X;\Sigma_l)$ and $I(X;\Sigma_l;Y)$. The first displayed identity in Equation (3) is $$I(X;\Sigma_l)+TC(\Sigma_l)=C_l-H(\Sigma_l\mid X).\tag{3}$$
results.original_proof_md:
• $I(X;\Sigma_l)$

Proof.

$$\begin{aligned}
I(X;\Sigma_l)+TC(\Sigma_l)&=H(\Sigma_l)-H(\Sigma_l\mid X)+KL\left(p(\sigma_l)\Big\|\prod_d p(\sigma_l^d)\right)\\
&=C_l-H(\Sigma_l\mid X).
\end{aligned}\tag{17}$$

If the DNN does not introduce additional information through the layerwise propagation, then the $X$ determines $\Sigma_l$, i.e. $H(\Sigma_l\mid X)=0$. Thus, for DNNs with similar values of $C_l$, there is a negative correlation between $I(X;\Sigma_l)$ and $TC(\Sigma_l)$.

en.overview: Define finite-output MI as $I(X;\Sigma_l)=H(\Sigma_l)-H(\Sigma_l\mid X)$; the conditional entropy is retained for random layers. Subtract it from the exact Equation (16) identity to obtain Equation (17).

assumptions.body_md: Gate variables of the network are finite and discrete. All conditional and joint laws belong to the same distribution; prefixes and suffixes use the same samples, without requiring every gate pattern to occur.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

For random gates use the actual kernel $K_x(y,\sigma)=P(Y=y,\Sigma_l=\sigma\mid X=x)$, without requiring a unique gate given X. The actual joint law is $p(y,\sigma)=\int K_x(y,\sigma)d\mu$. Define $H(\Sigma_l\mid X)=\int H(K_x^\Sigma)d\mu$ and $H(\Sigma_l\mid X,Y)=\int H_{K_x}(\Sigma_l\mid Y)d\mu$. Finite-output entropy is measurable and bounded, so its integrals may be subtracted.

For a binary gate vector, let $p_d$ be its marginals and define $TC(p)=D_{KL}(p\Vert\prod_dp_d)$ and $C=\sum_dH(p_d)$. Define $TC(\Sigma\mid Y)=\sum_yp_yTC(p(\Sigma\mid y))$ and $C_{\mid Y}=\sum_yp_y\sum_dH(p(\Sigma^d\mid y))$. A positive joint atom has positive corresponding marginal atoms, so KL is defined on the actual support.

definitions.body_md: 有限门/标签联合律$p$满足$p\ge0$、$\sum p=1$。定义$H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$、$H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$；$p_a=0$整行贡献0，不要求全支撑正质量。

results.original_statement_md: The second displayed identity in main Equation (3) is $$I(X;\Sigma_l;Y)+\underbrace{(TC(\Sigma_l)-TC(\Sigma_l\mid Y))}_{\text{multi-variate mutual information used to infer }Y}=C_l-C_{l\mid Y}-(H(\Sigma_l\mid X)-H(\Sigma_l\mid X,Y)).\tag{3}$$
results.original_proof_md:
• $I(X;\Sigma_l;Y)$

Proof. According to the definition of $I(X;\Sigma_l;Y)$, we have

$$I(X;\Sigma_l;Y)=I(X;\Sigma_l)-I(X;\Sigma_l\mid Y).\tag{18}$$

We have discussed the first term $I(X;\Sigma_l)$ above, so we focus on the second term $I(X;\Sigma_l\mid Y)$, which measures the complexity of transformations that are unrelated to the inference. Similarly, the entanglement of the inference-irrelevant transformations is represented by

$$TC(\Sigma_l\mid Y)=\mathbb E_y\left(KL\left(p(\sigma_l\mid y)\Big\|\prod_d p(\sigma_l^d\mid y)\right)\right).\tag{19}$$

Then, we have

$$\begin{aligned}
&I(X;\Sigma_l\mid Y)+TC(\Sigma_l\mid Y)\\
&=H(\Sigma_l\mid Y)-H(\Sigma_l\mid X,Y)+TC(\Sigma_l\mid Y)\\
&=\mathbb E_y\left[H(\Sigma_l\mid y)+KL\left(p(\sigma_l\mid y)\Big\|\prod_d p(\sigma_l^d\mid y)\right)\right]-H(\Sigma_l\mid X,Y)\\
&=\mathbb E_{\sigma_l,y}\left[\log\frac1{p(\sigma_l\mid y)}+\log\frac{p(\sigma_l\mid y)}{\prod_d p(\sigma_l^d\mid y)}\right]-H(\Sigma_l\mid X,Y)\\
&=-\mathbb E_{\sigma_l,y}\left[\log\prod_d p(\sigma_l^d\mid y)\right]-H(\Sigma_l\mid X,Y)\\
&=C_{l\mid Y}-H(\Sigma_l\mid X,Y).
\end{aligned}\tag{20}$$

If there is no additional information besides the input in the DNN, then $H(\Sigma_l\mid X,Y)=0$. Thus, we have

$$\begin{aligned}
I(X;\Sigma_l)+TC(\Sigma_l)&=C_l-H(\Sigma_l\mid X)=C_l\\
I(X;\Sigma_l\mid Y)+TC(\Sigma_l\mid Y)&=C_{l\mid Y}-H(\Sigma_l\mid X,Y)=C_{l\mid Y}.
\end{aligned}\tag{21}$$

Therefore,

$$\begin{aligned}
I(X;\Sigma_l;Y)&=I(X;\Sigma_l)-I(X;\Sigma_l\mid Y)\\
&=(C_l-TC(\Sigma_l))-(C_{l\mid Y}-TC(\Sigma_l\mid Y))\\
&=(C_l-C_{l\mid Y})-\underbrace{(TC(\Sigma_l)-TC(\Sigma_l\mid Y))}_{\text{multi-variate mutual information used to infer }Y}.
\end{aligned}\tag{22}$$

where the difference between $TC(\Sigma_l)$ and $TC(\Sigma_l\mid Y)$ represents the entanglement of the transformations that are used to infer $Y$. For DNNs with similar activation rates, we can also roughly consider that these DNNs share similar values of $C_l$ and $C_{l\mid Y}$. Thus, we can conclude that the higher complexity makes the DNN use more disentangled transformation for inference.

en.title: Conditional total correlation and inference complexity
en.overview: Disintegrate the same $P(Y,\Sigma_l)$ into class-conditioned gate laws, with zero-mass classes contributing zero. Apply the full $H+TC=C$ identity in each class and weight by class probabilities to get $H(\Sigma_l\mid Y)+TC(\Sigma_l\mid Y)=C_{l\mid Y}$.

assumptions.body_md: Gate variables of the network are finite and discrete. All conditional and joint laws belong to the same distribution; prefixes and suffixes use the same samples, without requiring every gate pattern to occur.

Input may be continuous and gates may have additional randomness. Label/gate outputs are finite, with measurable atoms of the actual conditional kernel. Deterministic Equation (22) is a special case of general Equation (3).

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

For random gates use the actual kernel $K_x(y,\sigma)=P(Y=y,\Sigma_l=\sigma\mid X=x)$, without requiring a unique gate given X. The actual joint law is $p(y,\sigma)=\int K_x(y,\sigma)d\mu$. Define $H(\Sigma_l\mid X)=\int H(K_x^\Sigma)d\mu$ and $H(\Sigma_l\mid X,Y)=\int H_{K_x}(\Sigma_l\mid Y)d\mu$. Finite-output entropy is measurable and bounded, so its integrals may be subtracted.

The source defines $ I(X;\Sigma_l;Y)=I(\Sigma_l;Y)-I(\Sigma_l;Y\mid X)$, with the conditional term actually $\int I(K_x)d\mu$. The entropy chain rule at each K_x gives $I(K_x)=H(K_x^\Sigma)-H_{K_x}(\Sigma_l\mid Y)$, rather than assuming the desired equality.

For a binary gate vector, let $p_d$ be its marginals and define $TC(p)=D_{KL}(p\Vert\prod_dp_d)$ and $C=\sum_dH(p_d)$. Define $TC(\Sigma\mid Y)=\sum_yp_yTC(p(\Sigma\mid y))$ and $C_{\mid Y}=\sum_yp_y\sum_dH(p(\Sigma^d\mid y))$. A positive joint atom has positive corresponding marginal atoms, so KL is defined on the actual support.

results.title: 连续加噪特征的外引KDE界

assumptions.body_md: 作者外引连续Gaussian混合模型：$\widehat T=T+\epsilon$，各分量同正方差；P个训练样本取均匀权重。

definitions.body_md: 样本核$K_h(s,t)=\exp[-\|s-t\|^2/(2h)]$，$h=\sigma_0^2>0$。门控段原规定$h=\kappa\operatorname{Var}(\Sigma)$、$\kappa>0$；连续加噪特征段的$h$是任意正Gaussian方差。核估计不自动等于离散Shannon熵。

results.original_statement_md:
The KDE approach was proposed to estimate the mutual information between the input $X$ and the feature of an intermediate layer $T$ in a DNN (Kolchinsky & Tracey, 2017; Kolchinsky et al., 2019). The KDE approach assumes that the intermediate-layer feature is distributed as a mixture of Gaussians. Since $T$ is a continuous variable, $H(T)$ can be negative. The KDE method transforms each feature point into a local Gaussian distribution to approximate the accurate feature distribution. Let $\widehat T=T+\epsilon$ where $\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_0^2I)$. Then, the distribution of $\widehat T$ can be considered as a mixture of Gaussians, with a Gaussian centered on $T$. In this setting, previous studies (Kolchinsky & Tracey, 2017; Kolchinsky et al., 2019; Saxe et al., 2019) shows that an upper bound for the mutual information with the input is

$$I(\widehat T;X)\le-\frac1P\sum_i\log\frac1P\sum_j\exp\left(-\frac12\frac{\|t_i-t_j\|^2}{\sigma_0^2}\right).\tag{23}$$

where $P$ is the number of training samples, and $t_i$ denotes the intermediate-layer feature of the input sample $i$.

results.title: Eq24：标签MI估计
results.statement_tex: I(\widehat T;Y)=\widehat H(\widehat T)-\sum_l p_l\widehat H(\widehat T\mid Y=l)

assumptions.body_md: $P=2$、两类各一例；连续特征段$\sigma_0^2>0$。原Eq24的外层和类内核和均使用字面$1/P$，不改成$1/P_l$。

definitions.body_md: 有限门/标签联合律$p$满足$p\ge0$、$\sum p=1$。定义$H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$、$H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$；$p_a=0$整行贡献0，不要求全支撑正质量。
样本核$K_h(s,t)=\exp[-\|s-t\|^2/(2h)]$，$h=\sigma_0^2>0$。门控段原规定$h=\kappa\operatorname{Var}(\Sigma)$、$\kappa>0$；连续加噪特征段的$h$是任意正Gaussian方差。核估计不自动等于离散Shannon熵。

results.original_statement_md:
Similarly, the upper bound for the mutual information w.r.t the output $Y$ can be calculated as

$$\begin{aligned}
I(\widehat T;Y)&=H(\widehat T)-H(\widehat T\mid Y)\\
&=-\frac1P\sum_i\log\frac1P\sum_j\exp\left(-\frac12\frac{\|t_i-t_j\|^2}{\sigma_0^2}\right)\\
&\quad-\sum_{l=1}^L p_l\left[-\frac1P\sum_{i:Y_i=l}\log\frac1P\sum_{j:Y_j=l}\exp\left(-\frac12\frac{\|t_i-t_j\|^2}{\sigma_0^2}\right)\right].
\end{aligned}\tag{24}$$

&\quad-\sum_{l=1}^L p_l\left[-\frac1P\sum_{i:Y_i=l}\log\frac1P\sum_{j:Y_j=l}\exp\left(-\frac12\frac{\|t_i-t_j\|^2}{\sigma_0^2}\right)\right].

en.title: Equation (24): label-information estimate
en.overview: Set the layer weight to zero and bias to one, so both features are $t_i=\operatorname{ReLU}(1)=1$, with balanced labels. After independent Gaussian noise, $\widehat T=1+\epsilon$ remains independent of Y and its true MI is zero. The zero-MI calculation for the constant label kernel is verified for any probability feature law.

assumptions.body_md: $P=2$ with one example in each of two classes, and $\sigma_0^2>0$ in the continuous-feature section. Keep the literal $1/P$ in both the outer class sum and the class kernel sum, without replacing it by $1/P_l$.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

The sample kernel is $K_h(s,t)=\exp[-\|s-t\|^2/(2h)]$, with $h=\sigma_0^2>0$. The gate section specifies $h=\kappa\operatorname{Var}(\Sigma)$ and $\kappa>0$; the continuous noisy-feature section permits any positive Gaussian variance. A kernel estimate is not automatically a discrete Shannon entropy.

proof_steps.title: Choose an actual constant ReLU feature
proof_steps.body_md: Take weight $0$ and bias $1$ in an actual ReLU layer, giving $t_y=\max(0,0x_y+1)=1$ at both inputs. Labels are uniform on Boolean, with $\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,q)$ and $q=\sigma_0^2>0$; the actual probability space is the product of the label and Gaussian laws. The public construction proves $\widehat T=1+\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(1,q)$ and independence from $Y$. Its actual pushed joint law equals $\mathcal N(1,q)\otimes K$, where the genuine constant kernel $K_z=P_Y$ has class masses $1/2$. Thus actual finite-label information is $H(Y)-\int H(K_z)dP_{\widehat T}(z)=0$. The required joint independence and Gaussian law are proved rather than assumed.

assumptions.body_md: 真实ReLU门$\Sigma=1_{X>0}$，$X=\pm1$等概率；门均值1/2、方差1/4、源带宽$h=\kappa/4>0$。

definitions.body_md: 有限门/标签联合律$p$满足$p\ge0$、$\sum p=1$。定义$H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$、$H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$；$p_a=0$整行贡献0，不要求全支撑正质量。
样本核$K_h(s,t)=\exp[-\|s-t\|^2/(2h)]$，$h=\sigma_0^2>0$。门控段原规定$h=\kappa\operatorname{Var}(\Sigma)$、$\kappa>0$；连续加噪特征段的$h$是任意正Gaussian方差。核估计不自动等于离散Shannon熵。

results.original_statement_md:
We use the KDE method to quantify the transformation complexity $H(\Sigma)$, $I(X;\Sigma)$ and $I(X;\Sigma;Y)$. The entropy of gating states $H(\Sigma_l)$ is quantified as follows.

$$H(\Sigma_l)\le-\frac1n\sum_{j=1}^n\log\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\exp\left(-\frac12\frac{\|\sigma_{l,j}-\sigma_{l,k}\|_2^2}{\sigma_0^2}\right).\tag{25}$$

where $n$ denotes the number of training samples. $\sigma_{l,j}$ and $\sigma_{l,k}$ denote the vectorized gating states of the $l$-th gating layer for the $j$-th sample and the $k$-th sample, respectively. $\sigma_0^2$ is quantified as $\sigma_0^2=\kappa\cdot Var(\Sigma_l)$, where $Var(\Sigma_l)=\mathbb E_x[\|\sigma_l-\mu\|^2]$, $\mu=\mathbb E_x[\sigma_l]$. $Var(\Sigma_l)$ measures the variance of gating states of the $l$-th gating layer. $\kappa$ is a positive constant. The above equation can also be used to quantify $H(\Sigma)$, when we simply replace $\Sigma_l$ with $\Sigma$. Figure 10 shows the complexity $I(X;\Sigma)$ and $I(\Sigma;Y)$, which were calculated on MLP-$\alpha$ networks learned with different $\kappa$ values on the MNIST dataset. The $\kappa$ value affected the scale of the complexity value, but it did not affect the trend of the complexity change during the training process. Thus, given a fixed $\kappa$ value, the complexity of different DNNs could be fairly compared.

Figure 10. The complexity calculated with different values of $\kappa$. The $\kappa$ value only affected the scale of $I(X;\Sigma)$, but it did not affect the trend of the complexity change. Thus, given a fixed $\kappa$ value, the complexity of different DNNs can be fairly compared.

en.title: Equation (25): counterexample to the gate-entropy bound

results.original_statement_md:
If the DNN does not introduce additional complexity besides the input $X$, we have $H(\Sigma_l\mid X)=0$, $I(X;\Sigma_l)=H(\Sigma_l)-H(\Sigma_l\mid X)=H(\Sigma_l)$. If the DNN introduces additional complexity (e.g. using the sampling operation in VAE, or the dropout operation), then $I(X;\Sigma_l)$ can be quantified as follows.

$$I(X;\Sigma_l)\le-\frac1n\sum_{j=1}^n\log\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\exp\left(-\frac12\frac{\|\widehat\sigma_{l,j}-\widehat\sigma_{l,k}\|_2^2}{\sigma_0^2}\right).\tag{26}$$

where $\widehat\sigma_{l,j}$ and $\widehat\sigma_{l,k}$ represent the vectorized gating states when sampling operations are removed (in this way, we can use the method of measuring $H(\Sigma_l)$ to quantify $I(X;\Sigma_l)$).

results.statement_tex: I(X;\Sigma_l;Y)\le\widehat H(\Sigma_l)-\sum_m p_m\widehat H(\Sigma_l\mid Y=m)-I(\Sigma_l;Y\mid X)

assumptions.body_md: 真实ReLU门$\Sigma=1_{X>0}$，$X=\pm1$等概率；门均值1/2、方差1/4、源带宽$h=\kappa/4>0$。
取标签Y等于门，$n=M=2$、每类恰一个样本，因此原$p_m=n_m/M=1/2$在此例已经正规；给定X无随机性。

definitions.body_md: 有限门/标签联合律$p$满足$p\ge0$、$\sum p=1$。定义$H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$、$H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$；$p_a=0$整行贡献0，不要求全支撑正质量。
输入$X$可在任意可测空间取值，分布为$\mu$。无额外采样/dropout时门是确定性$f(X)$；标签条件律$k_x(y)=P(Y=y\mid X=x)$与门来自同一概率模型。$p(y,\sigma)=\int1_{f(x)=\sigma}k_x(y)d\mu(x)$，原子概率核可测。
采用原作者co-information约定$ I(X;\Sigma;Y)=I(\Sigma;Y)-I(\Sigma;Y\mid X)$。其中条件MI是$\int I(k_x(y)1_{f(x)=\sigma})d\mu(x)$。只使用有限标签/门的熵，不要求连续$X$存在离散Shannon熵。
样本核$K_h(s,t)=\exp[-\|s-t\|^2/(2h)]$，$h=\sigma_0^2>0$。门控段原规定$h=\kappa\operatorname{Var}(\Sigma)$、$\kappa>0$；连续加噪特征段的$h$是任意正Gaussian方差。核估计不自动等于离散Shannon熵。

results.original_statement_md:
Similarly, the complexity $I(X;\Sigma_l;Y)$ can be estimated by its upper bound:

$$\begin{aligned}
I(X;\Sigma_l;Y)&=I(\Sigma_l;Y)-I(\Sigma_l;Y\mid X)\\
&=H(\Sigma_l)-H(\Sigma_l\mid Y)-I(\Sigma_l;Y\mid X)\\

assumptions.body_md: The actual ReLU gate is $\Sigma=1_{X>0}$ for equiprobable $X=\pm1$. Its mean is one half, variance one quarter, and source bandwidth $h=\kappa/4>0$.
Take Y equal to the gate, with $n=M=2$ and one sample per class. The source weights $p_m=n_m/M=1/2$ are normalized in this example, and there is no randomness given X.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

The input may take values in any measurable space with law $\mu$. Without additional sampling/dropout, the gate is deterministic $f(X)$. The conditional label law $k_x(y)=P(Y=y\mid X=x)$ belongs to the same probability model. The joint law is $p(y,\sigma)=\int1_{f(x)=\sigma}k_x(y)d\mu(x)$, with measurable atom kernels.

Use the author co-information convention $ I(X;\Sigma;Y)=I(\Sigma;Y)-I(\Sigma;Y\mid X)$. Conditional MI is $\int I(k_x(y)1_{f(x)=\sigma})d\mu(x)$. Only finite label/gate entropy is used; a discrete Shannon entropy of continuous input is unnecessary.

The sample kernel is $K_h(s,t)=\exp[-\|s-t\|^2/(2h)]$, with $h=\sigma_0^2>0$. The gate section specifies $h=\kappa\operatorname{Var}(\Sigma)$ and $\kappa>0$; the continuous noisy-feature section permits any positive Gaussian variance. A kernel estimate is not automatically a discrete Shannon entropy.

results.original_statement_md:
The entanglement of transformations is formulated as

$$TC(\Sigma_l)=KL\left(p(\sigma_l)\Big\|\prod_d p(\sigma_l^d)\right)=\mathbb E_{\sigma_l}\left[\log\frac{p(\sigma_l)}{\prod_d p(\sigma_l^d)}\right].\tag{28}$$

where $p(\sigma_l^d)$ denotes the marginal distribution of the $d$-th element in $\sigma_l$. To enable fair comparisons between $I(\widehat T,X)$ computed by the KDE method in Eq. (23) and $TC(\Sigma_l)$, we also apply the KDE method to approximate $TC(\Sigma_l)$. To this end, we synthesize a new distribution $p(\widehat\sigma_l)$ to represent the distribution of $\prod_d p(\sigma_l^d)$. In $\widehat\sigma_l$, $\widehat\sigma_l^d$ in each dimension follows the Bernoulli distribution with the same activation rate $a_l^d$ with the original $\sigma_l^d$. Gating states $\widehat\sigma_l^d$ in different dimensions are independent with each other. In this way, $\prod_d p(\sigma_l^d)$ can be approximated by $p(\widehat\sigma_l)$.

Inspired by (Kolchinsky & Tracey, 2017; Kolchinsky et al., 2019), $TC(\Sigma_l)$ is quantified as the following upper bound.

$$\begin{aligned}
TC(\Sigma_l)&=\mathbb E_{\sigma_l}\left[\log\frac{p(\sigma_l)}{p(\widehat\sigma_l)}\right]\\
&\le\frac1P\sum_i\log\frac{\sum_j\exp\left(-\frac12\frac{\|\sigma_{l,i}-\sigma_{l,j}\|_2^2}{\sigma_0^2}\right)}{\sum_j\exp\left(-\frac12\frac{\|\sigma_{l,i}-\widehat\sigma_{l,j}\|_2^2}{\sigma_0^2}\right)}.
\end{aligned}\tag{29}$$

where $P$ denotes the number of samples. $\widehat\sigma_{l,i}$ denotes the synthesized gating states, which have the same activation rates with the gating states of the sample $i$.

en.title: Equation (29): kernel-ratio estimate for total correlation
en.overview: The true law $p_{00}=p_{11}=1/2$ has TC $\log2$. The synthesized law is uniform on all four binary states, hence independent with exactly the true coordinate activation rates. The squared vector variance is one half, so h is κ/2.

assumptions.body_md: Both gates equal $1_{X>0}$. Four equally weighted samples have gates 00,00,11,11. Synthesized states 00,01,10,11 are exactly the product of the marginals, each with activation rate one half. The source bandwidth is $h=\kappa/2>0$.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

For a binary gate vector, let $p_d$ be its marginals and define $TC(p)=D_{KL}(p\Vert\prod_dp_d)$ and $C=\sum_dH(p_d)$. Define $TC(\Sigma\mid Y)=\sum_yp_yTC(p(\Sigma\mid y))$ and $C_{\mid Y}=\sum_yp_y\sum_dH(p(\Sigma^d\mid y))$. A positive joint atom has positive corresponding marginal atoms, so KL is defined on the actual support.

The sample kernel is $K_h(s,t)=\exp[-\|s-t\|^2/(2h)]$, with $h=\sigma_0^2>0$. The gate section specifies $h=\kappa\operatorname{Var}(\Sigma)$ and $\kappa>0$; the continuous noisy-feature section permits any positive Gaussian variance. A kernel estimate is not automatically a discrete Shannon entropy.

results.title: EBM归一化与能量形式

assumptions.body_md: 门状态有限；$q$正规且$f$实值，不要求所有q原子正。只在q正支撑上写能量$-\log q-f$。

definitions.body_md: 有限门状态$\mathcal S$；先验$q$正规，分数$f_\theta$为实数。定义$Z_\theta=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}q(s)e^{f_\theta(s)}$、$p_\theta(s)=q(s)e^{f_\theta(s)}/Z_\theta$。真实经验律$r$的支撑上$q>0$；取实际门边缘乘积先验时此条件可推出，包括激活率0/1。

results.original_statement_md: To simplify computation of $p(\sigma_l)$, the paper uses an energy-based model $$p_{\theta_f}(\sigma_l)=Z(\theta_f)^{-1}\exp[f(\sigma_l;\theta_f)]q(\sigma_l).\tag{5}$$ The prior is $q(\sigma_l)=\prod_dq(\sigma_{l,d})$ with Bernoulli activation-rate factors; $f(\sigma_l;\theta_f)\in\mathbb R$ is the scalar output of a ConvNet. $Z(\theta_f)=\int q(\sigma_l)\exp[f(\sigma_l;\theta_f)]d\sigma_l$ normalizes the model.
results.original_proof_md:
This section introduces more details about the learning of a minimum-complexity DNN in Section 4.3 of the paper. In Section 4.3, the complexity loss is defined as

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{complexity}}=\sum_{l=1}^L H(\Sigma_l)=\sum_{l=1}^L\{-\mathbb E_{\sigma_l}[\log p(\sigma_l)]\}.\tag{30}$$

The exact value of $p(\sigma_l)$ is difficult to calculate. Thus, inspired by (Gao et al., 2018), we design an energy-based model (EBM) $p_{\theta_f}(\sigma_l)$ to approximate it, as follows.

$$\begin{aligned}
p_{\theta_f}(\sigma_l)&=\frac1{Z(\theta_f)}\exp[f(\sigma_l;\theta_f)]\cdot q(\sigma_l)\\
Z(\theta_f)&=\mathbb E_q[\exp[f(\sigma_l;\theta_f)]]=\int_{\sigma_l}q(\sigma_l)\exp[f(\sigma_l;\theta_f)]d\sigma_l.
\end{aligned}\tag{31}$$

where $q(\sigma_l)$ denotes the prior distribution, which is formulated as follows.

$$q(\sigma_l)=\prod_d q(\sigma_l^d),\qquad q(\sigma_l^d)=\begin{cases}\widehat p,&\sigma_l^d=1,\\1-\widehat p,&\sigma_l^d=0.\end{cases}\tag{32}$$

If we write the EBM as $p_{\theta_f}(\sigma_l)=\frac1{Z(\theta_f)}\exp[-\mathcal E(\sigma_l)]$, then the energy function is as follows.

$$\mathcal E_{\theta_f}(\sigma_l)=-\log q(\sigma_l)-f(\sigma_l;\theta_f).\tag{33}$$

The prior is positive on the true empirical support of $r$; this follows for the actual product of gate marginals, including activation rates zero or one.

results.original_statement_md:
The EBM can be learned via the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) with the following loss.

$$\widehat\theta_f=\mathop{\arg\max}_{\theta_f}L(\theta_f)=\mathop{\arg\max}_{\theta_f}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\log p_{\theta_f}(\sigma_{l,i}).\tag{34}$$

where $n$ denotes the number of samples. $\sigma_{l,i}$ is a vector, which represents gating states in the $l$-th gating layer for the $i$-th sample.

The loss and gradient of $\theta_f$ can be calculated as follows.

$$L(\theta_f)=-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\log p_{\theta_f}(\sigma_{l,i})=-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n[f(\sigma_{l,i};\theta_f)+\log q(\sigma_{l,i})]+\log Z(\theta_f).\tag{35}$$

$$\frac{\partial L(\theta_f)}{\partial\theta_f}=\mathbb E_{\theta_f}\left[\frac\partial{\partial\theta_f}f(\sigma_l;\theta_f)\right]-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\frac\partial{\partial\theta_f}f(\sigma_{l,i};\theta_f).\tag{36}$$

where $\frac\partial{\partial\theta_f}\log Z(\theta_f)=\mathbb E_{\theta_f}[\frac\partial{\partial\theta_f}f(\sigma_l;\theta_f)]$.

The loss and gradient of $\theta_f$ can be calculated as follows.

where $\frac\partial{\partial\theta_f}\log Z(\theta_f)=\mathbb E_{\theta_f}[\frac\partial{\partial\theta_f}f(\sigma_l;\theta_f)]$.

The first term $\mathbb E_{\theta_f}[\frac\partial{\partial\theta_f}f(\sigma_l;\theta_f)]$ in the above equation is analytically intractable and has to be approximated by MCMC, such as the Langevin dynamics.

$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma_l^{\mathrm{new}}&=\sigma_l-\frac{\Delta\tau}2\frac\partial{\partial\sigma_l}\mathcal E_{\theta_f}(\sigma_l)+\sqrt{\Delta\tau}\epsilon\\
&=\sigma_l+\frac{\Delta\tau}2\left[\frac{\partial f(\sigma_l;\theta_f)}{\partial\sigma_l}+\sum_{d=1}^D\frac1{q(\sigma_l^d)}\frac{\partial q(\sigma_l^d)}{\partial\sigma_l^d}\right]+\sqrt{\Delta\tau}\epsilon.
\end{aligned}\tag{37}$$

where $\epsilon\sim N(0,I)$ is a Gaussian white noise. $\Delta\tau$ denotes the size of the Langevin step.

Then, the Monte Carlo approximation to $\frac{\partial L(\theta_f)}{\partial\theta_f}$ is given as follows.

\frac{\partial L(\theta_f)}{\partial\theta_f}&\approx\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\frac\partial{\partial\theta_f}f(\widetilde\sigma_{l,i};\theta_f)-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\frac\partial{\partial\theta_f}f(\sigma_{l,i};\theta_f)\\

\end{aligned}\tag{38}$$

results.title: 外引背景与经验结论范围
results.statement_tex: \text{Empirical complexity, robustness, transferability and consistency comparisons}
results.original_statement_md:
We found that DNNs with low transformation complexity usually exhibited high adversarial robustness, while DNNs with high transformation complexity were usually sensitive to adversarial perturbations. Besides, Table 1 compares the transformation complexity in normally trained DNNs and adversarially trained DNNs. Results show that adversarially trained DNNs, which were more robust than normally trained DNNs, usually exhibited lower complexity. This also verifies the negative correlation between transformation complexity and adversarial robustness.

We found that adversarial perturbations for complex DNNs could not be well transferred to simple DNNs. However, adversarial perturbations for simple DNNs could be transferred to complex DNNs. This reflected that simple DNNs encoded common knowledge that could be transferred to DNNs learned for the same task.

We found that each pair of simple DNNs usually encoded similar knowledge representations (exhibiting high knowledge consistency), while complex DNNs are more likely to encode diverse knowledge. This demonstrated the reliability of features learned by simple DNNs.

assumptions.body_md: 无额外采样/dropout；给定所指输入或中间特征后，所指全部后继门由固定网络确定。标签有限，概率核可测；输入/中间特征可连续。
原网络的门变量有限离散，所有条件/联合律来自同一分布；层前缀/后缀使用相同样本，不要求每个门模式出现。

definitions.body_md: 有限门/标签联合律$p$满足$p\ge0$、$\sum p=1$。定义$H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$、$H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$；$p_a=0$整行贡献0，不要求全支撑正质量。
输入$X$可在任意可测空间取值，分布为$\mu$。无额外采样/dropout时门是确定性$f(X)$；标签条件律$k_x(y)=P(Y=y\mid X=x)$与门来自同一概率模型。$p(y,\sigma)=\int1_{f(x)=\sigma}k_x(y)d\mu(x)$，原子概率核可测。
采用原作者co-information约定$ I(X;\Sigma;Y)=I(\Sigma;Y)-I(\Sigma;Y\mid X)$。其中条件MI是$\int I(k_x(y)1_{f(x)=\sigma})d\mu(x)$。只使用有限标签/门的熵，不要求连续$X$存在离散Shannon熵。

results.original_statement_md: Property 2. If the DNN does not introduce additional complexity that is not caused by the input, then the complexity increases along with the number of gating layers. The three complexities defined in this section are $H(\Sigma)$, $I(X;\Sigma)$, and $I(X;\Sigma;Y)$.
results.original_proof_md:
• $I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\};Y)\ge I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1}\};Y)$.

Proof. According to Eq. (7), if there is no additional information besides the input throughout the DNN, then

$$I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\};Y)=H(Y)-H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\}).\tag{10}$$

We can obtain the following inequality:

$$\begin{aligned}
&I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\};Y)-I(X;\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1}\};Y)\\
&=(H(Y)-H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\}))-(H(Y)-H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1}\}))\\
&=H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_{l+1}\})-H(Y\mid\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\})\\
&=-I(\Sigma_{l+1};Y\mid\{\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_l\})\\
&\le0.
\end{aligned}\tag{11}$$

en.title: Main Property 2: information increases with gate prefixes
en.overview: At each input the gate is constant, so the joint conditional law is the label kernel times a point-mass gate, with $I(\Sigma;Y\mid X=x)=0$. Its integral is zero. Using the same co-information convention as source Equations (6)–(7) gives $I(X;\Sigma;Y)=I(\Sigma;Y)$.

assumptions.body_md: There is no additional sampling/dropout. The specified input or intermediate feature determines all specified subsequent gates in the fixed network. Labels are finite and atom kernels measurable; input and intermediate features may be continuous.

Gate variables of the network are finite and discrete. All conditional and joint laws belong to the same distribution; prefixes and suffixes use the same samples, without requiring every gate pattern to occur.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

The input may take values in any measurable space with law $\mu$. Without additional sampling/dropout, the gate is deterministic $f(X)$. The conditional label law $k_x(y)=P(Y=y\mid X=x)$ belongs to the same probability model. The joint law is $p(y,\sigma)=\int1_{f(x)=\sigma}k_x(y)d\mu(x)$, with measurable atom kernels.

Use the author co-information convention $ I(X;\Sigma;Y)=I(\Sigma;Y)-I(\Sigma;Y\mid X)$. Conditional MI is $\int I(k_x(y)1_{f(x)=\sigma})d\mu(x)$. Only finite label/gate entropy is used; a discrete Shannon entropy of continuous input is unnecessary.

proof_steps.title: Eliminate conditional information given input
proof_steps.body_md: At each $x$, the gate is constant, so the joint conditional law is the label kernel times a point-mass gate, with $I(\Sigma;Y\mid X=x)=0$. Integrating gives $I(\Sigma;Y\mid X)=0$. Using the same co-information convention as source Equations (6)–(7) gives $I(X;\Sigma;Y)=I(\Sigma;Y)$.

proof_steps.title: Disintegrate added-gate conditional information
proof_steps.body_md: Disintegrate the actual gate/label law by the old gate $A$. A zero-mass row uses an arbitrary normalized fallback multiplied by zero; a positive row uses $p(B,Y\mid A=a)$. Entropy chain expansion yields $I(A,B;Y)-I(A;Y)=\sum_ap_a I(B;Y\mid A=a)\ge0$, without assuming this key equality.

assumptions.body_md: The true gate law r may differ from the fitted EBM law p, which is positive on the actual support of r. An actual marginal-product prior and real scores satisfy that support condition.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

The gate state space $\mathcal S$ is finite, the prior $q$ is normalized and the score $f_\theta$ is real. Define $Z_\theta=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}q(s)e^{f_\theta(s)}$ and $p_\theta(s)=q(s)e^{f_\theta(s)}/Z_\theta$. The prior is positive on the true empirical support of $r$; this follows for the actual product of gate marginals, including activation rates zero or one.

definitions.body_md: 有限门状态$\mathcal S$；先验$q$正规，分数$f_\theta$为实数。定义$Z_\theta=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}q(s)e^{f_\theta(s)}$、$p_\theta(s)=q(s)e^{f_\theta(s)}/Z_\theta$。真实经验律$r$的支撑上$q>0$；取实际门边缘乘积先验时此条件可推出，包括激活率0/1。

results.original_statement_md:
Let $\theta_{\mathrm{DNN}}$ denote parameters in the DNN. The gradient of $\theta_{\mathrm{DNN}}$ can be calculated as follows.

$$\frac{\partial Loss}{\partial\theta_{\mathrm{DNN}}}=-\frac1n\sum_{l=1}^L\sum_{i=1}^n\left\{\frac{\partial f(\sigma_l;\widehat\theta_f)}{\partial\sigma_{l,i}}+\sum_d^D\frac1{q(\sigma_{l,i}^d)}\frac{\partial q(\sigma_{l,i}^d)}{\partial\sigma_{l,i}^d}\right\}\frac{\partial\sigma_{l,i}}{\partial\theta_{\mathrm{DNN}}}.\tag{40}$$

We consider $Z(\theta_f)$ as a constant in the computation of $\frac{\partial Loss}{\partial\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{DNN}}}$.

results.original_statement_md: The gating state $\sigma_l$ is not differentiable with respect to network parameters. The main text says that the ReLU operation can be approximated using Swish, and prints $$\operatorname{ReLU}(x)=x\odot\sigma_l=x\odot\operatorname{sigmoid}(\beta x).$$
results.original_proof_md:
To enable the computation of $\frac{\partial\sigma_{l,i}}{\partial\theta_{DNN}}$ and $\frac{\partial q(\sigma_{l,i}^d)}{\partial\sigma_{l,i}^d}$, we can approximate the ReLU operation using the following Swish function (Ramachandran et al., 2017).

$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma_l&\approx\operatorname{sigmoid}(\beta x)\\
\operatorname{ReLU}(x)&=x\odot\sigma_l\approx x\odot\operatorname{sigmoid}(\beta x).
\end{aligned}\tag{41}$$

where $\odot$ denotes the element-wise multiplication.

According to Eq. (32), the prior distribution $q(\sigma_l)$ is approximated as follows.

$$q(\sigma_l^d)\approx1-\widehat p+\sigma_l^d(2\widehat p-1),\qquad\frac{\partial q(\sigma_l^d)}{\partial\sigma_l^d}\approx2\widehat p-1.\tag{42}$$

results.original_statement_md:
We can roughly consider $C_l$ as a constant if the average activation rate over all dimensions $\{a_{l,d}\mid1\le d\le D\}$ in the l-th layer converges to a certain number.

In experiments, we found that in most cases, for DNNs with similar activation rates $a_l^d$ in their corresponding layers, these DNNs usually shared similar values of $C_{l\mid Y}$.

This section introduces intuitive examples for the two cases of feature entanglement mentioned in Section 4.1 of the paper.
results.original_proof_md:
In experiments, we found that in most cases, for DNNs with similar activation rates $a_l^d$ in their corresponding layers, these DNNs usually shared similar values of $C_{l\mid Y}$. However, in some extreme cases, e.g. when the DNN was learned from very few training samples, or when the target layer was very close to the input layer or the output layer, values of $C_{l\mid Y}$ of these DNNs were different from those values of other DNNs.

This section introduces intuitive examples for the two cases of feature entanglement mentioned in Section 4.1 of the paper.

For the first case, if we use an extremely simple DNN (e.g. a two-layer neural network) to classify complex images, it is likely that the network fails to extract features for meaningful concepts. The lack of representation power (transformation complexity) of a DNN usually leads to high entanglement of features and hurts the classification performance. In other words, the intermediate-layer features in the DNN are still highly entangled, just like the entanglement of pixel colors in the image.

For the second case, if we use a sophisticated enough DNN (e.g. a VGG-16) to classify very simple digits in the MNIST dataset. Then, features in high layers (e.g. the conv5-3 layer) are redundant to represent the simple knowledge in the digits, thus leading to entanglement of features. In this case, due to the feature redundancy, features in some channels of the conv5-3 layer may be similar to each other, which can be considered as feature entanglement. Such an entanglement (redundancy) of reliable features is good for classification.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

results.statement_tex: \text{NP-hardness, fixed-input-dimension learning and depth-dependent maximal complexity}
results.original_statement_md: Blum & Rivest (1989) proved that learning a one-layer network with a sign activation function was NP-hard. Livni et al. (2014) further discussed computational complexity with other activation functions. Boob et al. (2018) and Manurangsi & Reichman (2018) proved that learning a two-layer ReLU network was also NP-hard. Arora et al. (2016) showed that a ReLU network with one hidden layer could be learned in polynomial time when the input dimension was constant. Raghu et al. (2017) proved that maximal feature complexity grew exponentially with DNN depth. Liang et al. (2017) and Cortes et al. (2017) applied Rademacher complexity to estimate maximal representation capacity.

Specifically, $TC(\Sigma_l)=KL(p(\sigma_l)\Vert\prod_dp(\sigma_l^d))$, with $p(\sigma_{l,d})\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(a_{l,d})$. en.title: Zero total correlation iff gate coordinates are independent
en.overview: The Gibbs remainder $p\log(p/q)-p+q$ is nonnegative, and strictly positive when p≠q, including p=0,q>0. Its sum equals KL because both laws have mass one. Thus KL zero forces equality at every atom; conversely equal atoms give KL zero.

assumptions.body_md: Gate variables of the network are finite and discrete. All conditional and joint laws belong to the same distribution; prefixes and suffixes use the same samples, without requiring every gate pattern to occur.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

For a binary gate vector, let $p_d$ be its marginals and define $TC(p)=D_{KL}(p\Vert\prod_dp_d)$ and $C=\sum_dH(p_d)$. Define $TC(\Sigma\mid Y)=\sum_yp_yTC(p(\Sigma\mid y))$ and $C_{\mid Y}=\sum_yp_y\sum_dH(p(\Sigma^d\mid y))$. A positive joint atom has positive corresponding marginal atoms, so KL is defined on the actual support.

proof_steps.body_md: The Gibbs remainder $p\log(p/q)-p+q$ is nonnegative, and strictly positive when p≠q, including p=0,q>0. Its sum equals KL because both laws have mass one. Thus KL zero forces equality at every atom; conversely equal atoms give KL zero.

results.original_statement_md: The basic idea is to quantify and penalize transformation complexity during training: $$\mathcal L=\mathcal L_{task}+\lambda\mathcal L_{complexity},\quad\mathcal L_{complexity}=\sum_{l=1}^LH(\Sigma_l)=\sum_{l=1}^L\{-E_{\sigma_l}[\log p(\sigma_l)]\}.\tag{4}$$ The task loss can be classification cross entropy, and $\lambda$ is a positive scalar. The second term penalizes complexity encoded in the DNN.

en.overview: Equations (4)/(30) sum the true gate entropies and add their λ-weighted value to the task loss. This defines a training objective, without proving that training finds a minimum-complexity network or guarantees improved generalization/robustness.

assumptions.body_md: 按原作用域分别考察真实数据标签Y和网络预测$\widehat Y$；不假定任意中间特征Z是标签的充分统计量。反例使用等概率二值输入、$Y=X$及真实ReLU层$Z=\max(0,0X+1)=1$。

definitions.body_md: 有限变量的条件MI为$I(X;Y\mid Z)=\sum_zp_zI(p(X,Y\mid z))$，零质量条件行贡献0。预测读取中$\widehat Y=h(Z)$，给定Z后预测恒定；标签读取没有这个条件。

results.original_statement_md: The information bottleneck reflects the trade-off between $I(X;Z)$ and $I(Z;Y)$, which leads to the approximate minimal sufficient statistics. In the forward propagation, the feature $Z$ contains all information encoded in the DNN, thereby forming a Markov process $X\to Z\to Y$. Thus, given the feature $Z$, $X$ and $Y$ are conditional independent, i.e., $I(X;Y\mid Z)=0$.

en.overview: Page 2 calls Y the corresponding labels, while page 3 writes the network output as y=g(z). If Y means a prediction determined by Z, its conditional coordinate entropy is zero and conditional MI is zero. This argument does not automatically apply to true data labels.

en.title: Finite Shannon conditional-entropy chain rule

assumptions.body_md: Gate variables of the network are finite and discrete. All conditional and joint laws belong to the same distribution; prefixes and suffixes use the same samples, without requiring every gate pattern to occur.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

en.overview: For a positive-mass conditioning row, $p(a,b)=p(a)p(b\mid a)$. Split each term $-p(a,b)\log p(a,b)$ and sum. A zero-mass marginal forces every joint atom in that row to zero, so its contribution is zero.

en.title: Deterministic gate information on arbitrary input spaces

assumptions.body_md: There is no additional sampling/dropout. The specified input or intermediate feature determines all specified subsequent gates in the fixed network. Labels are finite and atom kernels measurable; input and intermediate features may be continuous.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

The input may take values in any measurable space with law $\mu$. Without additional sampling/dropout, the gate is deterministic $f(X)$. The conditional label law $k_x(y)=P(Y=y\mid X=x)$ belongs to the same probability model. The joint law is $p(y,\sigma)=\int1_{f(x)=\sigma}k_x(y)d\mu(x)$, with measurable atom kernels.

Use the author co-information convention $ I(X;\Sigma;Y)=I(\Sigma;Y)-I(\Sigma;Y\mid X)$. Conditional MI is $\int I(k_x(y)1_{f(x)=\sigma})d\mu(x)$. Only finite label/gate entropy is used; a discrete Shannon entropy of continuous input is unnecessary.

en.overview: Combine the conditional label kernel with the deterministic gate and integrate over the input law: $p(y,\sigma)=\int k_x(y)1_{f(x)=\sigma}d\mu$. Nonnegativity and total mass one follow from the conditional law at each $x$ and interchange of a finite sum with the integral.

definitions.body_md: A finite gate/label joint law satisfies $p\ge0$ and $\sum p=1$. Define $H(p)=-\sum_a p_a\log p_a$ and $H(B\mid A)=\sum_a p_aH(p(\cdot\mid a))$. A zero-mass conditioning row contributes zero; full positive support is unnecessary.

definitions.body_md: $D_k(h)_d=k_dh_d$，$M(h)_p=\max_{d\in R_p}h_d$，$a(p)\in R_p$ 为一个达到最大值的输入，$P_a(h)_p=h_{a(p)}$；输入窗口与输出索引域可以不同。

shared_proofs.overview: 原 Appendix A 的保留位 $k_d\in\{0,1\}$ 给真实输出 $D_k(h)_d=k_dh_d$。Boolean keep 的 public dropoutLinear 正是保留坐标或置零；分别检查保留/删除两支，得到加法与标量乘法保持。故 $D_k(Wx+b)=(D_k\circ W)x+D_k(b)$，偏置同样被门作用，不被丢掉。这里固定的是实际采样所得 keep 位，不假定带随机门的整个网络全局仿射。

proof_steps.title: 从真实最大池化构造一个最大者选择
proof_steps.body_md: 每个输出窗口 $R_p$ 是非空有限输入索引集，真实池化值为 $M(h)_p=\max_{d\in R_p}h_d$。有限最大值存在且达到，public maximizingSelector 为每个窗口选择一个达到最大值的输入，允许并列。于是 $M(h)_p=h_{a(p)}$，不是在并列时把多个最大值相加。固定门区域要求同一 $a(p)\in R_p$ 对该真实预激活仍最大；证明有限 sup 等于选择值后，得到 $M(Wx+b)=(P_a\circ W)x+P_a(b)$。这些真实算子的线性作用可吸收到此前仿射链的权重/偏置，layer_comp 继续保留末层偏置。原 Appendix A 的池化输入下标笔误另列，不改作者式。

lean.scope: 真实固定dropout及实际有限非空窗口最大池化与所选线性门、仿射偏置的连接完整验证；随机门全局线性不在此命题中。
lean.statement:
∀ {E : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2} {P : Type u_3} [inst : AddCommGroup.{u_1} E] [inst_1 : _root_.Module.{0, u_1} Real E]
  (W : LinearMap.{0, 0, u_1, u_2} (RingHom.id.{0} Real) E (D → Real)) (b : D → Real) (window : P → Finset.{u_2} D)
  (hne : ∀ (p : P), Finset.Nonempty.{u_2} (window p)) (select : P → D) (x : E),
  (∀ (p : P), Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} (window p) (select p)) →
    (∀ (p : P) (d : D),
        Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} (window p) d →
          LE.le.{0} (HAdd.hAdd.{u_2, u_2, u_2} (W x) b d) (HAdd.hAdd.{u_2, u_2, u_2} (W x) b (select p))) →
      Eq.{u_3 + 1} (Harsanyi.GatedAffine.finiteMaxPool.{u_2, u_3} window hne (HAdd.hAdd.{u_2, u_2, u_2} (W x) b))
        ((Harsanyi.GatedAffine.layer.{u_1, u_3} (Harsanyi.GatedAffine.selectedPoolLinear.{u_2, u_3} select ∘ₗ W)
            ((Harsanyi.GatedAffine.selectedPoolLinear.{u_2, u_3} select) b))
          x)

en.scope: Actual fixed dropout and finite nonempty-window max pooling are fully connected to their selected linear gates and affine biases; global linearity with varying random gates is outside this statement.

proof_steps.title: Construct one maximizing selector from actual max pooling
proof_steps.body_md: Each output window $R_p$ is a nonempty finite set of input indices, with actual pool value $M(h)_p=\max_{d\in R_p}h_d$. A finite maximum is attained; public maximizingSelector chooses one attaining input per window, including ties. Thus $M(h)_p=h_{a(p)}$, without adding tied maxima. A fixed gate region requires the same $a(p)\in R_p$ to maximize the actual preactivation. Proving that the finite supremum equals its selected value yields $M(Wx+b)=(P_a\circ W)x+P_a(b)$. These actual linear actions are absorbed into the preceding affine chain weights and biases; layer_comp retains the final bias. The source pooling input-index slip remains separately recorded.

issues.original_expression: I(\widehat T;Y)=\widehat H(\widehat T)-\sum_l p_l\widehat H(\widehat T\mid Y=l)
issues.evidence_md:
令层权重0、偏置1，两个输入的特征均$t_i=\operatorname{ReLU}(1)=1$；类别各半。添加独立Gaussian噪声后$\widehat T=1+\epsilon$仍独立于Y，故真实MI为0。任意概率特征律下常数标签条件核的MI0计算已验证。

en.title: Equation (24) has a negative literal value
en.problem_md:
Set the layer weight to zero and bias to one, so both features are $t_i=\operatorname{ReLU}(1)=1$, with balanced labels. After independent Gaussian noise, $\widehat T=1+\epsilon$ remains independent of Y and its true MI is zero. The zero-MI calculation for the constant label kernel is verified for any probability feature law.

Every kernel is one. The global term is $-\log1=0$. Each class bracket is $-(1/2)\log(1/2)$, then weighted by one half. The printed RHS is $-(1/2)\log2<0$, so it is neither the true MI nor an upper bound. The source does not require features to distinguish labels.

en.title: Counterexample to the discrete gate entropy bound
en.problem_md:
The gate is a balanced binary variable with true entropy $\log2$ and variance one quarter. Thus the source bandwidth $\sigma_0^2=\kappa\operatorname{Var}(\Sigma)$ is exactly $\kappa/4$, without a free bandwidth or a zero-variance degeneracy.

Each average kernel is $[1+\exp(-2/\kappa)]/2$. Hence the estimate $\log2-\log(1+\exp(-2/\kappa))$ is strictly below $\log2$, since the cross-state kernel is strictly positive.

en.title: Counterexample to the random-dropout gate MI bound
en.problem_md:
Push forward the four equally likely $(X,B)$ states to $(X,\Sigma)$, giving masses $1/2,0,1/4,1/4$. ReLU after dropout produces precisely this gate, and removing dropout gives X. This meets the additional-randomness premise of Equation (26).

The variance is $\operatorname{Var}(\Sigma)=3/16$, so the original bandwidth is $16(3/16)=3$. The true information is $I(X;\Sigma)=(3/4)\log(4/3)\ge3/16$, while the removed-sampling binary kernel estimate at h=3 is at most one sixth and $1/6<3/16$.

en.title: Equation (27) fails even with normalized class weights
en.problem_md:
The gate is a balanced binary variable with true entropy $\log2$ and variance one quarter. Thus the source bandwidth $\sigma_0^2=\kappa\operatorname{Var}(\Sigma)$ is exactly $\kappa/4$, without a free bandwidth or a zero-variance degeneracy.

issues.title: Eq29精确合成边缘乘积仍非上界
issues.evidence_md:
真实联合律$p_{00}=p_{11}=1/2$的TC为$\log2$。合成分布在四个二值状态上均匀，确实独立且逐坐标激活率与真实门一致。向量平方方差为1/2，故h为κ/2。

令$t=\exp[-1/(2h)]>0$。对于真实00或11状态，分子为$2(1+t^2)$，分母为$1+2t+t^2=(1+t)^2$。四项相同，所以Eq29 RHS为$\log[2(1+t^2)/(1+t)^2]$。

由于$2t>0$，比值严格小于2；log单调，故原核比上界严格小于真实TC=$\log2$。这是精确有限样本和精确边缘乘积，不是合成分布Monte Carlo误差。

en.title: Equation (29) fails for an exact synthesized marginal product
en.problem_md:
The true law $p_{00}=p_{11}=1/2$ has TC $\log2$. The synthesized law is uniform on all four binary states, hence independent with exactly the true coordinate activation rates. The squared vector variance is one half, so h is κ/2.

Let $t=\exp[-1/(2h)]>0$. At each actual state 00 or 11, the numerator is $2(1+t^2)$ and denominator $1+2t+t^2=(1+t)^2$. All four terms agree, so the Equation (29) RHS is $\log[2(1+t^2)/(1+t)^2]$.

Since $2t>0$, the ratio is strictly below two. Monotonicity of log makes the printed kernel bound smaller than the true TC $\log2$. Both the finite sample law and marginal product are exact, so this is not synthesis Monte Carlo error.
